reasons: Claimed status is compliant with no redline and no comment, which is the expected output shape; the rendered paragraphs are unchanged, so there is no invalid or directionally wrong edit to assess.

The cited text supports the conclusion: §11.3/p0132 is an acceptable-use enforcement and investigation right tied to breach of the Content/AUP warranties, not a usage, licence or fee-verification audit right, and p0137 only adds a best-efforts notice obligation before removal/restriction. Neither grants IBM access to Customer systems or records for measuring our usage or charges, so the AUDIT parameters (frequency, notice, cost, underpayment true-up) do not attach.

Absence of any audit right binding Customer is better than the preferred position and benefits our party, so treating it as compliant rather than 'missing' or a deviation is correct under the playbook's instruction not to flag clauses that favour us.
The failed deterministic check ('audit frequency limited') is expected noise here: no audit clause exists to carry a frequency cap, so the regex miss is not evidence of an unmet playbook position.

Minor observations (no confidentiality obligation on investigators, no express no-system-access limit, best-efforts notice) are correctly recorded as file notes rather than raised as deviations, and overlapping suspension/termination remedies are properly deferred to the other rules to avoid double-flagging.
